name: Abraço
sum: Tiny, beloved espresso bar that coffee people make pilgrimages to. Order, sip at the counter or on the sidewalk, go.
love: Some of the best espresso in the city
The olive oil cake is famous
watch: Lines spill onto the sidewalk on weekends

name: La Cabra
sum: Copenhagen roaster's NYC bakery-café. Light, precise coffee and cardamom buns people line up for.

name: Coffee Project NY
sum: The original tiny shop, famous for its deconstructed latte flight and creative signature drinks.
love: Deconstructed latte is a fun, giftable experience

name: Coffee Project NY (Chelsea)
sum: The roomier sibling of the East Village original, with the same signature drinks and space to open a laptop.
love: Much more seating than the original

name: Variety Coffee (Chelsea)
sum: Reliable, affordable neighborhood roaster where laptops are welcome and nobody rushes you.

name: Seven Grams Caffe
sum: Clean, bright café that remote workers cite for strong wifi and space to settle in.
watch: Coffee is good but not a destination

name: Felix Roasting Co.
sum: Lavishly designed café with dessert-like signature lattes. Half coffee shop, half photo shoot.
love: Creative drinks (the s'mores latte gets raves)
watch: Crowded and loud at peak times

name: Think Coffee (Mercer St)
sum: Big, NYU-adjacent workhorse café with long tables and a mission-driven sourcing story.
watch: Packed with students during the semester

name: Stumptown (Greenwich Village)
sum: Portland roaster's West 8th St café: dependable espresso and a classic third-wave room.

name: Café Integral
sum: Small café focused on Nicaraguan coffee, from a founder with family roots in coffee farming.
love: Calm compared to SoHo spots nearby

name: Ground Support
sum: SoHo staple on West Broadway with a sidewalk bench made for people-watching.

name: Maman (SoHo)
sum: French-country café with a full food menu and a famous nutty chocolate chip cookie.
love: The cookie lives up to the hype
watch: Coffee is fine, not the main event
Not a laptop spot at brunch

name: Caffe Reggio
sum: Opened in 1927, this old-world MacDougal St café is said to have served America's first cappuccino.
love: Open late, great for a post-dinner date

name: Partners Coffee (West Village)
sum: Brooklyn roaster's cozy West Village café, with seasonal drinks and quality espresso.

name: 787 Coffee (West Village)
sum: Puerto Rican coffee grown on the company's own farm, at friendly prices, with free wifi throughout.

name: Fasan Coffee
sum: LES café with thrift-shop charm and big people-watching energy.

name: After Eden
sum: Vietnamese coffee shop on the LES. Think phin drip, coconut and egg coffees.
love: Something you can't get at a typical café

name: Ludlow Coffee Supply
sum: Easygoing LES spot with room to sit and a laid-back, creative crowd.
love: Good for an hour or two of work

name: Culture Espresso
sum: Midtown's go-to for real coffee near Bryant Park, with famous chocolate chip cookies.
love: Best coffee in a coffee-desert area
watch: Packed at morning and lunch rush

name: Bibble & Sip
sum: Tiny bakery-café known for matcha drinks and cream puffs, near the Theater District.
drink: Lavender earl grey latte or matcha latte

name: Black Fox Coffee (FiDi)
sum: Polished Financial District café rotating guest roasters, a rare great cup downtown.

name: Birch Coffee (Flatiron)
sum: Long-running local chain with a homey feel and a book-lined vibe at its original Flatiron spot.

name: Irving Farm (Upper West Side)
sum: Hudson Valley roaster's UWS café with a real kitchen and room to linger.
love: Good for a long meeting or work block

name: The Hungarian Pastry Shop
sum: Columbia-adjacent institution where writers and grad students have hunkered down for decades. No wifi.
love: Sidewalk tables across from the cathedral
drink: Cappuccino + a pastry from the case

name: Café Lalo
sum: Dessert-café made famous by You've Got Mail, with an enormous cake menu and late hours.

name: Lenox Coffee
sum: Harlem neighborhood anchor with a warm community feel and room to work.

name: Remi Flower & Coffee
sum: Flower shop and coffee bar in one. A pretty pocket of calm in Midtown East.

name: Ralph's Coffee (Fifth Ave)
sum: Ralph Lauren's café: a preppy, green-and-white set piece with merch.

name: The Elk
sum: West Village café-boutique with a sought-after breakfast menu.

name: Café Grumpy (Chelsea)
sum: Long-running roaster café, historically a no-laptop zone (status to verify).

name: Devoción
sum: Colombian roaster with famously fresh beans in a soaring, skylit greenhouse of a space.

name: SEY Coffee
sum: Light-roast specialists in a bright, airy Bushwick space. A temple for coffee nerds.

name: Sweatshop
sum: Australian-style café with a strong flat white and toasties.

name: Variety Coffee (Williamsburg)
sum: The original Variety: a dependable, affordable spot where laptops are the norm.

name: Café Grumpy (Greenpoint)
sum: The Greenpoint original: roomy, relaxed, and good for settling in.

name: Odd Fox
sum: Small Greenpoint coffee bar with serious espresso.

name: Bakeri
sum: Norwegian-style bakery with rustic charm, known more for bread and pastries than coffee.

name: Brooklyn Roasting Company
sum: Big, industrial DUMBO café with plenty of room and a steady laptop crowd.

name: Burly Coffee
sum: Small neighborhood favorite with quality espresso and friendly regulars.

name: Little Zelda
sum: Tiny, charming Franklin Ave espresso bar.

name: Breukelen Coffee House
sum: Spacious, community-minded café on Franklin Ave, good for working.
watch: Coffee is good, not a destination

name: Café Regular du Nord
sum: Tiny European-style café with old-world charm.

name: Café Beit
sum: Laid-back Bushwick café with a backyard and plenty of laptop real estate.

name: Café Erzulie
sum: Haitian-inspired café by day, bar and party space by night, with a garden out back.

name: Antilles Cafe
sum: Flatbush café recently added to Time Out's best-coffee list.

name: Apartment Ra'el
sum: Concept store and coffee shop in Bed-Stuy, newly on Time Out's best-coffee list.

name: Win Son Bakery
sum: Taiwanese-American bakery-café with an all-day menu people line up for.

name: Hungry Ghost (Fort Greene)
sum: Local chain serving Stumptown-style espresso, with a dependable work-friendly setup.

name: Sit & Wonder
sum: Neighborhood café on Washington Ave with a backyard and a low-key regulars crowd.

name: Café con Libros
sum: Intersectional feminist bookstore and café, as much a community space as a coffee stop.

name: Sweetleaf
sum: LIC pioneer known for its Rocket Fuel iced coffee and cozy, record-filled room.
love: Rocket Fuel cold coffee is iconic

name: Kinship Coffee
sum: Astoria's specialty favorite, roasting in-house with a friendly, laptop-OK room.

name: Milk & Pull
sum: Neighborhood café straddling Ridgewood and Bushwick, cheap and cheerful.

name: Topos Bookstore Café
sum: Used bookstore with a small café inside. Quiet, browse-y, slow.

name: The Carnegie Cigar Club And Lounge

Royal Bank Of Canada: For The World
Cha Cha Matcha (Located Inside Moynihan Train Hall)
Library Bar At Sheraton New York Times Square
The Bistro (Courtyard By Marriott Times Square)
